item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
908
ABNT20 KNHC 240520
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
upgraded Tropical Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest
of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic (AL90):
An area of low pressure located a few hundred miles south-southeast
of the Cabo Verde Islands is accompanied by a large area of
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. This system could become a
short-lived tropical depression later today or on Friday while it
moves northwestward to northward. However, strong upper-level winds
should end the opportunity for development by the weekend.
Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands should monitor the progress of
this system as gusty winds, areas of heavy rain, and flash flooding
are possible there by Friday.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Fay are issued under WMO
header WTNT31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT1.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fay are issued under WMO
header WTNT21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT1.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.description:

000

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...FAY MOVING WESTWARD OVER THE CENTRAL ATLANTIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM GMT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.8N 40.5W
ABOUT 955 MI...1540 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 40.5 West. Fay is moving
toward the west near 7 mph (11 km/h). A generally westward motion
with some decrease in forward speed is expected over the next few
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some slight strengthening is possible over the next day or so, with 
gradual weakening expected thereafter.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 240835
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
Convection has continued to burst in pulsing bands around the 
low-level circulation of Fay this morning. Subjective and objective 
satellite intensity estimates remain around 30-35 kt, which is 
consistent with the scatterometer pass from the previous advisory. 
Based on these estimates and the relatively steady state of the 
convective organization, the initial intensity is held at 35 kt for 
this advisory.
 
The storm is estimated to be moving at an estimated motion 270/6 kt.
A generally westward motion at a slightly slower forward speed is
expected to continue during the next few days while Fay is steered
along the southern periphery of a mid-level ridge located to the
north. The NHC track forecast is essentially an update of the
previous one, as the track model guidance remains tightly clustered.
 
Fay is traversing sea surface temperatures around 27-28C in an
environment of low vertical wind shear. However, the system is
embedded within a dry air mass, which should prevent significant
strengthening. In about 24-48 hours, vertical wind shear is forecast
to increase, which should cause the system to gradually weaken and
limit deep convection. At that time, Fay is forecast to become a
post-tropical cyclone. The NHC intensity forecast is similar to the
previous advisory and lies near the consensus aids.
